name: Intellect Design Arena Ltd
title: Intellect Design Arena Ltd - 538835 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Intellect's LTM income up 17% to ₹3,388 cr with Q2 at ₹878 cr, but the transcript shows no capacity or capex signal, and the pipeline grew only 9% with a lost SaaS customer and a heavy-promotion tone.

summary.headline: Intellect Design Arena Q2 FY27: LTM income up 17% to ₹3,388 crore, Q2 income ₹878 crore with EBITDA margin 22.7%, and a ₹13,125 crore pipeline up 9%.
summary.overview: Management framed Q2 around MSOCK, a newly launched system that makes enterprise knowledge computable and is used internally on 141 implementations. Trailing-twelve-month income rose 17% year-on-year, with license-linked income up 18% to ₹1,768 crore, and 25 institutions went live (up from 16 in Q1). Q2 income was ₹878 crore, with EBITDA of ₹199 crore and PAT of ₹104 crore, and cash and equivalents rose 31% year-on-year to ₹1,216 crore. Management pointed to a ₹850 crore quarterly run-rate as a new baseline and reiterated a ₹4,000 crore FY28 target, while the call also covered one lost SaaS customer and a JV licence sale that flatter the quarter.

financial_highlights.metric: LTM non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA (ex stock comp)
LTM PBT / PBT before exceptional items

segments.name: License-linked (license + AMC)
segments.commentary: Q2 license-linked income ₹457 crore; LTM ₹1,768 crore, up 18% YoY, now 52% of income. Management said license-linked revenue is growing faster than the base.

segments.name: Platform
segments.commentary: LTM platform income ₹591 crore, up 51% YoY and about half of the LTM growth. Q2 platform income ₹133 crore.

segments.name: AMC
segments.commentary: LTM AMC income ₹603 crore, up 12% YoY. Q2 AMC ₹160 crore. Management said AMC is typically about 20% of implementation contract value and starts once go-live completes.

segments.name: Implementation / customisation (A2)
segments.commentary: Management said customisation accounts for 48% of the implementation segment. Customisation revenue is recognised within implementation and does not convert into AMC.

guidance_outlook: Management said it is confident of Q4 income above ₹900 crore and a PBT guidance, citing a new ₹850 crore quarterly baseline sustained in Q1 and Q2 (the Q4 level was ₹850 crore).
FY28 income target of ₹4,000 crore reaffirmed. Chairman said he sees visibility of ₹5,000 crore for the company, though he declined to forecast FY28 numbers.

Chairman's margin sensitivity: if income rises from ₹850 crore to ₹950 crore with costs at ~₹700 crore, roughly ₹250 crore of EBITDA would imply about 27% margin; reaching ₹1,100-1,200 crore would move margin toward Temenos-type levels of ~32%.
Mainframe-to-cloud deals are expected to be upwards of double-digit millions of dollars each; timing could be 12 or 24 months.
Q3 FY27 one-time impact from the lost SaaS customer quantified by Rajesh Saxena at roughly US$300,000-400,000.
capex_capacity: R&D LTM: ~₹230 crore expensed through P&L and ~₹170 crore capitalised. Q2 specifically: ~₹54 crore expensed and ~₹42-43 crore capitalised.
Delivery capacity: 141 MSOCK-based internal implementations; management said a typical 12-month project can be delivered in about 8 months.

Accelerated programmes: a 15-month wealth programme in Asia, an 11-month programme for a Middle East client, and a European lending transformation advanced by three months; management is designing large programmes for 12-14 months against an industry norm of 18-24 months.
Management said the product-led organisation is being redesigned into a market-led one, and the CEO spent about 90 days on MSOCK positioning.
demand_pricing: Pipeline ₹13,125 crore, up 9% YoY and about 3x LTM income; 103 deals: 29 above ₹50 crore, 35 between ₹30-50 crore, 39 between ₹20-30 crore.

Q2 wins: 21 deals, up from 7 in Q1 (Q1 base as stated). Of these, 7 were AI-led and 9 came from the Americas and Europe, about half of new signings. 8 pipeline conversions in Q2 against 7 in Q1; 15 in H1.
Newer deals increasingly combine an upfront license with multi-year annual subscription fees.
Competitors: C3.AI and CORE AI for Purple Fabric; CAST for mainframe-to-cloud (described as parsing-based). Management named Temenos and Oracle FSS as head-to-head rivals in banking.
Management said MSOCK is subscription-based, with partnership, royalty, and exclusive partnership models under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue recognition for licence plus customisation deals, and whether customisation converts into AMC.
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Jain said the revenue is classified as A1 (license), A2 (implementation, including customisation), and A3 (AMC). Customisation stays in implementation and does not move to AMC. The CFO was asked to take the detailed accounting question offline.

qa_highlights.question: R&D bifurcation for Q2 and LTM.
qa_highlights.answer: LTM R&D ~₹230 crore expensed and ~₹170 crore capitalised. Q2 ~₹54 crore expensed and ~₹42-43 crore capitalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 an inflection point, and is the ₹4,000 crore FY28 target intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Jain said yes, citing MSOCK and a ₹13,000 crore pipeline; cost base flat at ~₹680 crore; ~₹40 crore of an extra ₹50 crore quarterly income would flow to margin. He reaffirmed ₹4,000 crore by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin not expanding despite the AI investment, and the case for a margin roadmap.
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Jain said ₹100 crore a year is being spent on AI internally rather than being shown as a profit line, and that AI plus eMACH is helping retain ~80% of the base. He pointed to cost containment at ~₹680-700 crore and margin levers as income grows.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the lost SaaS customer impact and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Jain said it was a contract term expiring after an acquisition, a planned ~20% churn in the base; the timing depends on when the new vendor is ready and could take 2-3 quarters. Rajesh Saxena put the Q3 impact at roughly US$300,000-400,000.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company consider a share buyback given the valuation and cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Jain said buyback was discussed at Board level but capital is prioritised for acquisitions in Latin America, Europe and Eastern Europe. Strategy head Vikas Misra is evaluating acquisitions of a certain size.

qa_highlights.question: Is MSOCK an extension of Enterprise Knowledge Graph (EKG), and how much frontier-model use is involved?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Jain said MSOCK is a second generation of EKG (vectorisation-based) with 39 patents filed. It uses a frontier model for only ~30% of processing; the bank's knowledge stays in the client environment. MSOCK is currently used to improve delivery margins, not billed separately.

risks_watch: Lost SaaS customer migrating out at contract expiry: impact not yet quantified beyond Q3 estimate; timing depends on the new vendor's readiness.
Q2 headline includes a JV licence sale to Fintel (UK); excluding it, management did not give a figure, and an analyst's estimate of ~8% YoY growth was not confirmed by management.
Organic growth and profit growth have been flat for several years per one analyst; management's 17% LTM figure is the basis for guidance, and Q2 margins rely on the ₹850 crore run-rate holding.
Mainframe-to-cloud and MSOCK revenue are early-stage; management said timing of ₹850 crore to ₹1,100 crore income depends on 12- or 24-month execution.
Monetisation model of MSOCK (subscription, royalty, partnership) not yet settled; a Technology Day was promised but not yet scheduled.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the numbers and strategy, with the Chairman dismissing quarter-on-quarter comparisons and pushing the LTM figure. Evasive on specifics where asked: he declined to forecast FY28 income, deferred the SaaS churn quantification, and passed the revenue-recognition and buyback questions to the CFO or said the Board had only discussed it.
key_quotes: Our trailing-twelve-month income is up 17% and has risen in each of the seven quarters on an LTM basis.
We are transforming the company into an AI company without taking any third-party capital and without diluting equity.

growth.why: Management reiterated the ₹4,000 crore FY28 target and is confident of Q4 income above ₹900 crore off an ₹850 crore quarterly baseline, backed by a ₹13,125 crore pipeline (up 9% YoY), 21 Q2 wins and a cost base flat at ~₹680 crore, though no new capacity was quantified and the ₹4,000 crore target is not tied to specific capacity.
